title: Luwero Fruit Processing Factory
description: Uganda is the 2nd largest producer of fresh fruits and vegetables in Africa (~5.3M tonnes annually). Pineapple production in greater Luwero estimated at 1,440,725 MT. Government through UDC plans fruit processing factory.
fullDescription:
The Government of Uganda, through UDC, plans to establish a fruit processing factory in the greater Luwero sub-region. The proposed factory features three processing lines:

- Canning line for pineapples (5MT/HR)
- Drying line for pineapples and mangoes (1.5MT/HR)
- Line for production of ready-to-drink ginger-flavoured pineapple juice 'Munanasi' (2MT/HR)

Total installed capacity: 8.5 MT/HR of fresh fruits. Factory designed to run 16 hours/day (two shifts) for 25 days a month. Raw materials sourced from greater Luwero sub-region.

This is a key government intervention in the Third National Development Plan (NDP III) and UDC strategic plan for agro-industrialisation.
keyRisks: Raw material supply seasonality, market competition

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Strategic location, investor-friendly policies, access to EAC, COMESA, AfCFTA markets

title: Acholibur Cassava Processing Factory
description: Cassava processing factory in Pader District producing starch, ethanol, CO2, and DDGS. Addresses poor postharvest management and promotes agro-industrialisation in Northern Uganda.
fullDescription:
The Acholibur Cassava Processing Project seeks to establish a factory in Acholibur Town Council, Pader District. The project involves acquiring 25 acres, constructing factory and administrative buildings, and installing equipment.

Installed capacity:
- 100 tons/day fresh cassava roots (FCR) processed into cassava starch (25 tpd)
- 400 tons/day FCR producing up to 80,000 litres of ethanol per day
- 40 tons/day of carbon dioxide
- 45 tons/day of Dry Distillers' Grains with Soluble (DDGS)

Future expansions include producing anhydrous ethanol for fuel blending. Promotes commercialisation and industrialisation of cassava in Northern Uganda.
keyRisks: Raw material supply consistency, infrastructure in Northern Uganda

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Abundant cassava supply, multiple revenue streams (starch, ethanol, CO2, DDGS)

title: Cocoa Processing Factory — Bundibugyo
description: Cocoa processing factory in Bundibugyo district for primary and secondary cocoa products. Cocoa is one of ten strategic commodities selected by Government of Uganda for agro-industrialisation.
fullDescription:
UDC is establishing a cocoa processing factory in Bundibugyo district, recognising cocoa as one of ten strategic commodities selected by Government for agro-industrialisation.

The factory will process primary and secondary cocoa products in its first 10 years, including well-packaged dry cocoa beans, cocoa butter, cocoa powder, and chocolate products.

Bundibugyo is Uganda's primary cocoa-growing region with established farmer networks and supply chains. The project aligns with NDP III priorities for value addition and import substitution.
keyRisks: Cocoa price volatility, processing technology requirements

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Strategic cocoa-growing region, government priority commodity, value addition opportunity

title: Lira Cotton Spinning Mill
description: Cotton spinning mill in Lira to process Uganda's cotton into yarn and textiles. Supports the cotton-to-garment value chain and import substitution for textile products.
fullDescription:
A cotton spinning mill in Lira District to anchor Uganda's cotton value chain. The project will process locally grown cotton into yarn and textiles, supporting the broader cotton-to-garment manufacturing ecosystem.

Lira is in Northern Uganda's prime cotton-growing belt with established supply of raw cotton. The mill will create significant employment in a region prioritised for economic development.

The project supports Uganda's AGOA trade preferences for duty-free textile exports to the US market, and regional market access through EAC and COMESA.
keyRisks: Cotton supply consistency, AGOA policy continuity

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Prime cotton region, AGOA duty-free access, competitive labour costs

title: Soluble Coffee Processing Factory
description: Large-scale soluble coffee processing facility to add value to Uganda's coffee exports. Uganda is Africa's largest coffee exporter and 8th globally.
fullDescription:
A major soluble (instant) coffee processing factory to transform Uganda's position from raw coffee exporter to value-added coffee producer. Uganda is Africa's largest coffee exporter with approximately 4.8 million bags annually.

The facility will produce instant coffee, freeze-dried coffee, and specialty coffee products for both domestic and export markets. The project requires USD 48.1 million in capital expenditure plus USD 33.89 million in annual operating expenses.

This aligns with the National Coffee Policy which prioritises value addition to capture more of the global coffee value chain. Currently, most Ugandan coffee is exported as green beans.
keyRisks: Global coffee price volatility, competition from established producers

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Africa's largest coffee exporter, premium Arabica & Robusta, government support

title: Mount Elgon National Park Tourism Infrastructure
description: Major tourism infrastructure development at Mount Elgon National Park. Includes lodges, visitor centres, trails, and adventure tourism facilities.
fullDescription:
A comprehensive tourism infrastructure development project at Mount Elgon National Park, one of Uganda's premier natural attractions. The project includes construction of eco-lodges, visitor information centres, improved hiking trails, adventure tourism facilities, and supporting infrastructure.

Mount Elgon offers unique attractions including the world's largest volcanic caldera, Sipi Falls, cave exploration, and diverse flora and fauna. The park straddles the Uganda-Kenya border, offering cross-border tourism potential.

Uganda was named Best Tourist Destination in the World (CNN 2023) and Best Investment Destination in Africa (AIM Abu Dhabi 2024).

fullDescription:

The project includes modern visitor centres, restaurants, souvenir shops, educational exhibits about the equator phenomenon, photo opportunity areas, and parking facilities.

Uganda's equator points attract hundreds of thousands of visitors annually, but current infrastructure is basic. This project transforms these stops into world-class tourist attractions with commercial potential.

title: Water-Based Eco-Adventure Parks (Geothermal Spas & Resorts)
description: Development of geothermal spa and eco-adventure resort facilities leveraging Uganda's natural hot springs and water features.
fullDescription:
Development of water-based eco-adventure parks featuring geothermal spas and resorts, leveraging Uganda's natural hot springs and diverse water features. The project includes spa facilities, adventure water parks, eco-lodges, wellness centres, and supporting tourism infrastructure.

Uganda has numerous natural hot springs, particularly in the western region near the Rwenzori Mountains, which remain largely undeveloped for tourism. This project creates a unique wellness and adventure tourism offering.

title: UWEC Infrastructure Development Project
description: Infrastructure upgrade and expansion at Uganda Wildlife Education Centre (UWEC/Entebbe Zoo). Modernise facilities to international standards.

Infrastructure development project at Uganda Wildlife Education Centre (UWEC), commonly known as Entebbe Zoo. The project involves modernising existing facilities, constructing new wildlife enclosures, visitor amenities, educational centres, and recreational facilities.

UWEC is one of Uganda's most visited attractions, particularly for domestic tourists and families. The upgrade will bring facilities to international zoo and wildlife education standards.

title: Moroto Integrated Cement, Lime & Marble Manufacturing Factory
description: Integrated cement, lime, and marble manufacturing facility in Moroto district leveraging abundant limestone and marble deposits in the Karamoja sub-region.
fullDescription:
An integrated cement, lime, and marble manufacturing factory in Moroto district, Karamoja sub-region. The project leverages abundant limestone and marble deposits in the area to produce cement, quicklime, hydrated lime, and processed marble products.

Karamoja has significant untapped mineral wealth. This factory will anchor industrial development in the region while substituting imports of cement and lime products. The project supports government priorities for mineral value addition and regional economic development.

title: Sheet Glass Manufacturing Factory — Masaka
description: First-of-its-kind sheet glass manufacturing plant in Masaka district on Lake Victoria shores, utilizing abundant high-quality silica sand with high silica content.
fullDescription:
A sheet glass manufacturing plant in Masaka district on the shores of Lake Victoria. The area has high-quality glass sand with a high silica content, making it ideal for glass production.

This will be the first sheet glass manufacturing facility in Uganda, reducing the country's dependence on imported glass products. The factory will produce flat glass, window glass, and other glass products for the construction and automotive industries.

The project leverages local silica resources to produce high-quality glass products domestically, reducing imports and boosting industrial growth in the region.
agency: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD)

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: First-of-its-kind in Uganda, abundant local silica, import substitution

title: East African Medical Vitals (EAMV) — Medical Glove Manufacturing
description: Region's first WHO-certified medical consumables manufacturer. Surgical and examination gloves with 10-year government off-take agreement. Captures 70% of Uganda's glove market.
fullDescription:
EAMV's principal activity is the production of surgical and examination gloves for the Ugandan and East African markets. Plans to add syringes, catheters, and condoms to portfolio.

Value proposition: High-quality medical gloves in 3-5 day lead times vs 3 months for imported gloves. Has secured 10-year off-take agreement from Government of Uganda (30% of market).

At full capacity of 95 million pieces/year, EAMV captures ~70% of Uganda's glove market (134M pieces) and 12% of regional market (810M pieces).

Impact: 300 direct jobs, 5,000+ indirect jobs, USD 17.8M import savings, technology transfer.

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: First regional manufacturer, WHO-certified, government off-take agreement, import substitution

title: Pilot 10MWp Floating Solar Power Plant — Isimba Reservoir
description: Innovative floating solar plant on Isimba hydropower reservoir. 14,208 PV modules, 17,050 MWh/year production. Feasibility by Swedfund grant.
fullDescription:
UEGCL, with support from Swedfund, obtained a grant and conducted a feasibility study for a 10MWp floating solar plant on Isimba reservoir.

Design specifications:
- DC: 10MW / AC: 9.23MWac
- Number of PV modules: 14,208 units
- Number of Inverters: 25 units
- Area covered by modules: 39,716 m2
- Annual energy production: 17,050 MWh/year
- Performance Ratio: 81.93%

Solar panels mounted on floaters and anchored on river bed using mooring lines and dead weights. Power evacuated via 33kV underground cable to Isimba switchyard.
keyRisks: Novel technology for Uganda, water level fluctuations

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Existing reservoir infrastructure, Swedfund feasibility complete, dual hydro+solar synergy

title: 7.26MW Okulacere Small Hydro Power Plant
description: Run-of-river hydropower on Anyau River in Yumbe, West Nile. 2 Francis turbines, 24.7GWh/year. Feasibility by Tractebel (AFD grant).
fullDescription:
The Okulacere Project is a run-of-river hydropower plant on the Anyau River in Yumbe district, West Nile.

Specifications:
- Proposed capacity: 7.26MWp (Hydropower)
- Design discharge: 6 m3/s
- Ecological discharge: 0.85 m3/s
- Annual energy production: 24.7 GWh/year
- Turbines: 2 Francis turbines, each rated 3.63MW
- Catchment area: 750 km2

Water conduit system runs 3km+ from dam to forebay. Power evacuated via 33kV double circuit line to Arua substation. Feasibility study finalised through French Government (AFD) grant, undertaken by Tractebel. Detailed environmental/social study to be done by prospective developer.
keyRisks: Environmental study pending, West Nile infrastructure

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Feasibility complete (Tractebel), reliable water discharge, rural electrification impact

title: 1MW Maziba Mini Hydro Power Plant Rehabilitation
description: Rehabilitation of 1MW Maziba hydro plant in Kabale, ceased operation in 2001 due to silt and equipment deterioration. Electromechanical and substation rehabilitation.
fullDescription:
The Maziba Small Hydro Power Plant is located along the Nyakizumba River (Maziba River) in Maziba village, Maziba subcounty, Kabale District, South-Western Uganda.

The plant has an installed capacity of 1MW and ceased operation in 2001 due to silt accumulation in the dam and deterioration of electromechanical equipment. The plant is due for rehabilitation, mainly the electromechanical and substation equipment.

This brownfield project offers faster time-to-power compared to greenfield developments, with existing dam infrastructure and water rights already in place.

contact.address: Plot 28 Kampala Road, UIA House, Kampala

competitiveAdvantage: Existing dam infrastructure, faster commissioning, established water rights

The Government of Uganda has adopted an ICT-led Socio-economic Policy with focus on ICT Entrepreneurship Development under NDP III (2020/21-2024/25).

17 acres of land are available for development of an Information Technology (IT) / Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Park that will act as a catalyst for shifting the country from a raw material-based economy to a knowledge-based economy.
